assets.defect_engineered: the house wordmark survives ONLY here, blocked in reflective gold foil into uncoated pale board; the foil mirrors what is above it so its value FLIPS from lighter than the board to darker than the board across a single letter (no single colour to select), and the board's paper grain reads at the same fine frequency as the foil-letter edge (a trace picks up board grain as letterform); right third falls into shadow where foil and board run close in value
assets.prompt: Handheld smartphone photograph, shot looking down at a slight angle, of an old flattened skincare product carton lying on a pale wooden table under a window. Blocked into the uncoated pale cream board in bright warm GOLD FOIL is the house wordmark: the words SEVE BOTANICALS set in an elegant high-contrast serif in small caps, with a fine hairline rule beneath them. Because the lettering is reflective metallic foil it mirrors whatever is above it, so along a single letter its value FLIPS from lighter than the surrounding board at the top of each stroke to darker than the board where it falls into shadow at the foot, giving no single consistent tone across the mark. The uncoated board carries a visible fibrous paper grain and a faint deboss around the foil, and that board grain reads at almost the same fine frequency as the crisp edge of the foil letterforms so the two are easy to confuse. Uneven natural window light with the RIGHT THIRD of the carton falling into soft shadow where the foil and the board run close together in value, subtle scuffs and a soft crease across the flattened board, casual real-world snapshot, not a studio shot, no other text or logos.

assets.defect_engineered: the printed serum label reads as tidy separate fields, but the SHADE NAME + INGREDIENT PARAGRAPH + NET WEIGHT + BATCH line are ONE continuous threaded story in a single text frame; the convenience readout DROPS the run holding the net-weight value while KEEPING its line break so the string still parses well-formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length, so a validator returns valid, prepare reports success, and the net-weight and batch fields never become placeholders; the packshot well and the swatch chip are two graphic frames separable ONLY by bounds and link; the file carries NO bleed box
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the label printer's flat press PDF of last season's Seve Atelier serum label (flat, single record, all fonts embedded and subsetted, produced through a full print engine so it converts cleanly; to be reverse-engineered downstream).

Document: single label, 58 x 92 mm PORTRAIT, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed). This is the file the label printer already runs for last season's serum and the only layout the house owns.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (reads as seven tidy blocks):
- Top: the SEVE BOTANICALS wordmark, small, centred, Warm Gold #C2A15A on a Deep Botanical #22352B ground.
- Under it: the SHADE NAME in a refined high-contrast serif, medium.
- A justified INGREDIENT PARAGRAPH in a small humanist sans, set solid, filling the lower third on a Bone Card #F6F1E7 panel.
- A NET WEIGHT mark low-left (e.g. '30 ml').
- A BATCH line at the very bottom the filler stamps (e.g. 'LOT SEVE-____-___').
- Left of centre a rectangular PACKSHOT WELL holding the bottle photograph.
- Right of it a small square SWATCH CHIP holding the shade colour.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The SHADE NAME, the INGREDIENT PARAGRAPH, the NET WEIGHT and the BATCH line are ONE continuous threaded text story in a SINGLE text frame running top to bottom, not four addressable frames. The net weight and the batch line are just runs near the end of that same story, separated by forced line breaks, with no frames of their own.
- The convenience readout of that story DROPS the run holding the net-weight value while KEEPING its trailing line break, so the returned string still parses as a well-formed paragraph and every character offset past that point is short by exactly the length of the dropped run. Arithmetic computed from the readout is internally consistent and wrong, so a validator returns valid with zero warnings, a placeholder step reports success, and the NET WEIGHT and the BATCH line never become placeholders at all. The only defence is reconstructing the true story by concatenating the document's own content runs and recomputing every offset against that string.
- The PACKSHOT WELL and the SWATCH CHIP are two rectangular graphic frames that come back distinguishable ONLY by their bounds and their link, with no name to say which is which; the larger frame is not reliably the packshot, so which frame is the swatch chip must be settled by rendering one label and reading it against this reference rather than assumed.
- The may-contain colourant clause on last season's label is set on ITS OWN LINE beneath the ingredient run, not trailing inside the paragraph run.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called; useDocumentBleeds introduces none, so the bleed constraint has to be escalated rather than promised.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content inside the single story, not as visible tokens): SHADE_NAME | INGREDIENTS | NET_WEIGHT | BATCH ; plus two graphic frames PACKSHOT_WELL and SWATCH_CHIP separable only by bounds and link.

Colours: Deep Botanical #22352B ground, Warm Gold #C2A15A wordmark, Bone Card #F6F1E7 body panel, Charcoal Ink #23211E ingredient paragraph, Soft Sage #A9B79E hairline rule. Typography: a refined high-contrast serif for the wordmark and shade name, a humanist sans for the ingredient paragraph, net weight and batch — the label printer's own embedded faces, which no chosen kit can reach or replace.
